001_N: ["You're ninety-five years old, under hot studio lights, and a late-night TV host leans across the desk.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
002_N: ["So, Doctor. How many times have you hiccuped?",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
003_N: ["You open your mouth to answer, and your whole body jumps.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
004_N: ["The audience laughs. You've heard that laugh for sixty-seven years. Because you have never, not once, stopped hiccuping.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
006_N: ["So what if you got the hiccups, and they never went away?",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
007_N: ["Sounds impossible? It happened. In nineteen twenty-two, an American farmer named Charles Osborne lifted a three-hundred-and-fifty-pound hog, fell, and started to hiccup.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
008_N: ["He didn't stop for sixty-eight years. Today, that's you. Only you're a doctor.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
009_N: ["Let's go back to where it started. You're twenty-eight, on a night shift in the emergency room.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
010_N: ["Your favorite sound in the world is a heartbeat through your stethoscope. Remember that. It matters later.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
011_N: ["At four in the morning, a huge patient slides off a stretcher. You catch him. All three hundred and fifty pounds.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
012_N: ["Something inside you goes pop. You feel nothing. Then your chest jumps.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
013_N: ["You laugh it off. You're a doctor. You know exactly what a hiccup is.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
014_N: ["Your diaphragm, the big muscle under your lungs, twitches. Air rushes in, and a flap in your throat slams shut. That's the sound.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
015_N: ["Nobody knows for sure why we have them. One theory says it's left over from tadpoles, which close their throats like that to breathe through gills.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
016_N: ["Babies even hiccup in the womb, before they ever breathe air.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
017_N: ["By morning, the whole shift has a cure for you. Hold your breath. Sugar on a spoon. Drink water upside down.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
018_N: ["A nurse pops a paper bag right behind your head.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
019_N: ["Nothing works. You go home, fall asleep, and wake up to the same rhythm.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
020_N: ["After two days, it gets a medical name. Persistent hiccups. You've written that on patients' charts. Now it's your chart.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
021_N: ["After a month, a scarier name. Intractable. It means nothing stops it.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
022_N: ["You get a brain scan. A colleague taps the screen, at a tiny spot near the base of your brain.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
023_N: ["When you caught that patient, a blood vessel the size of a pin may have burst. Right in the spot that tells hiccups to stop.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
024_N: ["Osborne's doctor guessed the very same thing. And just like him, there's nothing anyone can cut out.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
025_N: ["So you hiccup. Twenty to forty times a minute. Day and night.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
026_N: ["Being a doctor gets weird. You lean in to listen to a patient's heart, and every few seconds, you both jump.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
027_N: ["You give up surgery. Nobody wants a scalpel in a hand that jerks forty times a minute.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
028_N: ["Eating is like jumping rope with a sandwich. So you blend everything. Breakfast, lunch, steak.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
029_N: ["The real Osborne wore out two blenders. You wear out three.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
030_N: ["First dates go badly. You lean in for a kiss, and headbutt her.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
031_N: ["But one woman doesn't mind. She says your hiccups are like a metronome. Five years later, your \"I do\" comes out in two pieces.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
032_N: ["But none of that is the real problem.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
033_N: ["The real problem is the number. Forty a minute is more than fifty thousand a day.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
034_N: ["Your ribs ache. Your chest is sore all the time, like a workout that never ends. Osborne said it himself: \"I get so sore, jerking all the time.\"",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
035_N: ["You fly to the best clinic in the country. A doctor gives you a mix of gases to breathe, and the hiccups stop.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
036_N: ["But you can't breathe that gas forever. Fifty hours later, they're back. Osborne's longest break ever was about fifty hours, too.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
037_N: ["Then the newspapers find you. Letters pour in. Four thousand of them, each with a cure.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
038_N: ["Pickle juice. Peanut butter. Standing on your head. You try them all.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
039_N: ["Osborne's friend once fired a shotgun behind his back. Osborne said: \"It scared me some, but it didn't scare the hiccups out of me.\"",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
040_N: ["In twenty twenty-one, scientists tested a special straw. Ninety-two percent of users said it stopped their hiccups. You're in the other eight.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
041_N: ["Hit subscribe if you've ever had hiccups for more than an hour. You're still way behind.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
042_N: ["Decades roll past. Your kids grow up to the rhythm. They learn to talk in the gaps between your hiccups.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
043_N: ["Your hair goes grey. You're the only doctor in town your patients can hear coming down the hall.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
044_N: ["Then, at eighty, your wife gets sick. And this time, you're the one sitting by the hospital bed.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
045_N: ["The room is silent, except for the monitor, and you. You keep apologizing for the noise.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
046_N: ["She squeezes your hand. \"Forty-seven years,\" she says, \"and I never once lost you in a crowd.\"",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
047_N: ["You stay with her all night. Hiccup by hiccup.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
048_N: ["Fifteen years later, you're on that TV show. Over four hundred million. The audience applauds. You bow, and hiccup.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
049_N: ["Then one morning, at ninety-six, you wake up, and something is wrong. The house is too quiet.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
050_N: ["You wait. A minute. Ten minutes. An hour. Nothing.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
051_N: ["After sixty-eight years, it's just gone. Nobody knows why. Not your doctors. Not you.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
052_N: ["And the silence is terrifying. Osborne once said: \"I don't know what it would be like not to have them.\"",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
053_N: ["You take your old stethoscope out of the drawer, and press it to your own chest.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
054_N: ["And for the first time in sixty-eight years, you hear it. Your favorite sound. Just a heartbeat. Nothing else.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
055_N: ["The real Charles Osborne's hiccups stopped in nineteen ninety. He died a year later, at ninety-seven.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
056_N: ["He was married twice, raised eight kids, and made the Guinness World Records for the longest attack of hiccups ever.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
057_N: ["He never found a cure. He just kept living, one hiccup at a time.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
058_N: ["So next time you get the hiccups, don't panic. Most stop in a few minutes. And you're only four hundred and thirty million behind.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
059_N: ["What's the weirdest hiccup cure you've ever tried? Tell me in the comments.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
060_N: ["And subscribe, because next time, the patient is a teenager who stayed awake for eleven days straight.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
